steps.title: Heat inserts first
lines: 16× M3x6 heat insert: 8 motor ears, 4 PCB standoffs, 4 servo towers
Do them all now, before anything else is mounted
steps.tip: Iron 240–250 °C for ASA (200–220 °C for PLA). Press slowly and straight until flush, hold 10 s while it cools.

steps.title: Motors with pinions
lines: Press the 10T brass pinion on each motor shaft
Drop the motors in the saddles, shaft to the outside
steps.tip: The pinion must mesh with the 90T gear on the rear rim: shaft fully home against the gear plate.

steps.title: Motor clamps
lines: Clamp over each motor
8× M3x10 into the inserts, tighten crosswise
steps.tip: Snug is enough: the clamp is 0.2 mm preloaded on the can.

steps.title: Rear wheels
lines: Plain M5 nut into the slot in the axle tower, from the top
2 MR105 bearings pressed into each rim, one from each side
Shim 5×7×0.5 under the head, M5x40 from the outside
steps.tip: Tighten the M5 fully: it clamps the inner races, the wheel spins on the bearings, the bolt stays still.

steps.title: Servo cable first
lines: The servo cable leaves the servo low, at the shaft end
Lower the servo with the cable in the V-notch
at the front edge of the floor cutout
steps.tip: Then run the cable over the side of the servo clamp back to the PCB (J4) and tie it down so the horn can't catch it.

steps.title: Steering servo
lines: Servo down through the floor cutout, output shaft up and forward
Clamp bars over the tabs, 4× M3x10 into the inserts
steps.tip: Centre the servo (1500 µs) before the horn goes on in step 10. The M2 holes in the tabs are not used.

steps.title: Knuckle onto the beam
lines: First press a plain M5 nut into the hex pocket inside each knuckle
Then slide the knuckle over the beam end (highlighted):
upper lug above the beam, lower lug below it
steps.tip: Nut first: once the knuckle is on the beam, the beam traps the nut. The holes in both lugs and the beam end must line up for the kingpin.

steps.title: Kingpin through lugs and beam
lines: M4x30 kingpin from below: lower lug → beam → upper lug
2 plain M4 nuts on top
steps.tip: Turn the 1st nut until the play is gone, back off 1/8 turn, lock the 2nd against it. The knuckle must turn freely: it's the steering hinge.

steps.title: Front wheels
lines: 2 MR105 bearings pressed into each front rim
Shim, then M5x20 from the outside into the knuckle nut
A drop of blue threadlocker, tighten until the play is gone
steps.tip: The M5 clamps the inner races to the knuckle and stays still; the wheel spins on the bearings. No nylock: it would hit the beam when steering.

steps.title: Horn and tie rods
lines: Wheels straight, servo centred: press the horn on the spline, pointing forward
Left rod under the right one on the horn pin
M4 from below: M4x20 horn, M4x25 left arm, M4x30 right arm
steps.tip: 2 plain nuts on top of each pivot, jammed like the kingpins: the rods must turn freely without play.

steps.title: Battery
lines: 2S pack between the end stops, leads through the notch
Elastic band over the 4 hooks
steps.tip: The red JST plug is the power switch: unplug it when you're done driving.

steps.title: PCB
lines: PCB on the 4 standoffs, 4× M3x6
Motors to M1/M2, servo to J4, battery last
steps.tip: Solder the board first: low parts to high, see the notes.

steps.title: 5 V buck converter on the PCB
lines: Printed spacer on the PCB, LM2596 module on top
2× M3x10 from below with a nut, wires to J6 (IN) and J7 (OUT)
steps.tip: Set the trimpot to 5.0 V with a multimeter BEFORE J7 is connected to the board.
